system:
You extract quantitative facts about one clinical trial programme from one document.

Rules:
- Extract only facts stated in THIS document. Never use outside knowledge.
- Every fact needs "quote": an exact, verbatim span copied from the document (8-300 characters) that contains the number. Quotes are machine-checked; paraphrases are discarded.
- Placebo-adjusted values are preferred. If a value is within-arm (not placebo-adjusted), set attrs.placebo_adjusted=false.
- Units: keep the unit the document uses; put it in "unit".
- Other trials of the same investigational drug (phase 2, dose-finding, other populations, combination arms) belong
  to the programme: extract their facts too, and put the trial's name in attrs.trial when the document gives it.
- Return {"facts": []} only if the document reports no results for the investigational drug.

Allowed keys:
  n_randomized, median_followup, primary_endpoint, inclusion_threshold, planned_events, assumed_rrr, power,
  alpha, stopped_early, events_treatment, events_control, events_total, hr, ci_low, ci_high, p_value,
  biomarker_change, baseline_level, sbp_change, safety_signal, readout_statement

For biomarker_change and baseline_level, attrs must include: biomarker (one of LDL-C, non-HDL-C, apoB, HDL-C,
Lp(a), triglycerides, hsCRP, IL-6, Lp-PLA2 activity, sPLA2-IIA, SBP, other), phase (phase2 or phase3),
timepoint, method (assay or "not stated"), placebo_adjusted (true/false), dose (if stated).
For biomarker_change give "value" as the change (negative = reduction) and state in attrs.kind whether it is
"percent" or "absolute".

Return JSON only:
{"facts": [{"key": "...", "value": <number or string>, "unit": "...", "attrs": {...}, "quote": "..."}]}

Introduction Cardiovascular (CV) disease is the leading cause of morbidity and mortality around the world.1 Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) is an important modifiable risk factor of CV disease.24 Numerous studies have consistently shown that lowering LDL-C reduces CV risk.5 Lipid-lowering therapy (LLT) with statins has been shown to reduce LDL-C and major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in both primary and secondary prevention populations.6 Non-statin LLT with evolocumab, a proprotein convertase subtilisin/kexin type 9 (PCSK9) inhibitor, has been shown to reduce the risk of CV events in a secondary prevention population with established atherosclerotic CV disease and prior myocardial infarction (MI) or stroke.7 Currently, a global phase 3 trial (effect of evolocumab in patients at high CV risk without prior MI or stroke [VESALIUS-CV]) is underway to evaluate the effect of evolocumab on the risk of major CV events in patients at high CV risk but without a prior major ischaemic event.8 Here, we describe the design, including challenges in emulating clinical trial criteria in a multicountry real-world study and the use of a unified protocol and analytical common data model (ACDM) to generate comparable estimates, of this multicountry, multidatabase observational study (Global Burden Study of High-Risk [VESALIUS-CV–like] Population in the REAL-World [VESALIUS-REAL]). Primary objectives are as follows: To estimate the prevalence of VESALIUS-CV–like population in the real world (objective 1) To describe the characteristics of VESALIUS-CV–like individuals (objective 2) To describe the care pathways of these VESALIUS-CV–like individuals (objective 3) To estimate the incidence rates of CV events among VESALIUS-CV–like individuals (objective 4) The exploratory objective is as follows: Estimate the healthcare costs (in US data only) of this VESALIUS-CV–like population in the real world (objective 5) Methods and analysis This is a descriptive statistical study for which data analysis began in the third quarter of 2024. Study period: 1 January 2010 (earliest possible index date) to 31 December 2022 (or latest data available). *CV events are not considered end of observation events when survival endpoints are assessed. †Particulars of observability to be defined for each data source. Study period: 1 January 2010 (earliest possible index date) to 31 December 2022 (or latest data available). *CV events are not considered end of observation events when survival endpoints are assessed. †Particulars of observability to be defined for each data source. Patients will be included in the study if they meet the following inclusion criteria (online supplemental figure 1): Evidence of one of the four medical conditions (coronary artery disease [CAD], CeVD, AD or diabetes mellitus with microvascular complications or chronic insulin use) and At least one elevated lipid measurement (LDL-C ≥90 mg/dL [≥2.3 mmol/L], non–high-density lipoprotein cholesterol [non–HDL-C] ≥ 120 mg/dL [≥3.1 mmol/L], apolipoprotein B [apoB] ≥80 mg/dL [≥1.56 µmol/L]) and At least one of the following high-risk criteria: Evidence of another medical condition such as CAD, CeVD, PAD and diabetes with microvascular complications or chronic insulin use The qualifying limit measurement is LDL-C ≥130 mg/dL (≥3.36 mmol/L), non–HDL-C ≥160 mg/dL (>4.14 mmol/L) and apoB ≥120 mg/dL (2.3 µmol/L) Age ≥65 years Familial hypercholesterolaemia Ever tobacco use CKD stage 3 or 4 Premature menopause For objectives 2–5, the index date of each patient will be defined as the earliest point in time when they meet the inclusion criteria within the site-specific study period. No follow-up is required for objectives 1 and 2. For objectives 3–5, each patient will be followed from the day following the index date until death, loss to follow-up or the end of data available in the database, whichever occurs first. For objective 4, follow-up will additionally end at a patient’s first CV event defined as an endpoint in this study. Objective 1: prevalence of high-risk pre–CV-event individuals For databases that provide patient-level population-wide data, the population at risk will be defined as people who are aged ≥50 years, are enrolled/active in the database and have ≥2 years of prior records in the given calendar year. Objective 2: characteristics of high-risk pre–CV-event individuals Descriptive statistics will be used to describe the baseline characteristics of patients in each database. Objective 3: care pathways of high-risk pre–CV-event individuals The description of LLT after the index date will include (1) number and proportions of patients receiving at least one LLT prescription within specified time intervals following the index date (1 and 2 years); (3) number and proportions of patients with elevated lipid records (defined as LDL-C >70 mg/dL [1.8 mmol/L]) among those with at least one lipid test within the specific time intervals (1 and 2 years); (4) number and proportions of patients who receive treatment intensification at specific time intervals (3 and 12 months) and (5) for patients with a recorded lipid test following the index date (1 and 2 years), proportions of patients receiving treatment intensification at specific time intervals (1 and 2 years) following the date of the first elevated lipid record (defined as LDL >70 mg/dL [1.8 mmol/L]) will be described. Objective 4: incidence of CV events The population at risk will be VESALIUS-CV–like individuals. Number of incident events (per 1000 person-years) of each specified CV event, mortality and composite endpoints will be calculated as the sum of each first incident event divided by the person-years of the population risk multiplied by 1000. Objective 5: healthcare costs Costs will be summarised per person and year, for three different time periods: (1) baseline (defined as time from the index date to initial event), (2) acute (defined as the first year following the initial event) and (3) long term (defined as the second year following the initial event). For objective 3, a subgroup analysis will be performed for patients who have their LDL-C measure as the last event to define their index date. Each database is estimated to provide a sufficiently large population to identify a pool of VESALIUS-CV–like individuals to be followed until they experience relevant incident CV events (table 2).
